context:
Goal: every idle session hands off and is archived, losing no work (owner, 09:18 CST Nov 10).
Problem (money): the only way to get their handoff is to read each transcript, and only a session, not an agent, can read one.
Based on (measured): the collector measured 12-15k tokens per transcript read, even filtered to assistant and result events, so 213 reads is about 3.2M tokens.
Based on (read): a session left live keeps its full transcript, so leaving one live loses no work.
Departs from: main (213 sessions with no stored handoff) — adds a stored handoff for some or all of them.
Meanwhile: the collector writes the 213 ids, titles and times to nr.txt on branch archive/session-handoffs-2026-11-10 and waits.

reply: Your answer, 10:50 CST Nov 10 (none of these): "retry sending a message again first, then after that those that fail can be read workflow style in haiku xhigh not sonnet". Re-asking all 213 now. At 11:30 CST the still-silent ones are read by Haiku helper sessions at effort xhigh, then archived. Departs from your words in one way: workflow agents cannot read sessions (hook agent-no-remote-tools), so the readers are Haiku sessions, not workflow agents. (Coordinator 10:51 CST; routed by triage 10:51 CST.)
title: 213 sessions never answered the handoff ask. How should their handoffs be collected?
why: Recent sessions are the likeliest to hold live work, and a session left live loses nothing.
